system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Energy Shock, AI Rivalry, and War
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, fast-moving web driven by overlapping crises: regional wars (Iran-Hormuz, Israel-Gaza, Russia-Ukraine) that are disrupting energy flows and raising geopolitical risk; a high-stakes great-power strategic competition centered on the U.S.-China relationship that now incorporates trade, Taiwan, the Arctic, and an accelerating AI race; and synchronized stress in global finance and commodity markets (soaring yields, diesel shortages) that amplify political pressures and policy volatility. These dynamics interact nonlinearly — energy shocks feed inflation and market turmoil, AI and tech-security concerns reshape diplomacy and industrial policy, and regional conflicts create feedbacks that alter alliances and economic flows.
system_description.scope: Sovereign states (major powers and regional actors), transnational institutions (UN, NATO, EU, IMF), cross-border markets (oil, diesel, metals, bonds, crypto), global tech/AI firms and standards processes, strategic military deployments and regional conflicts, and critical supply chains (energy, semiconductors, rare earths).
system_description.super_system: The integrated global political-economic-technical system (planetary-scale governance, markets, and socio-technical infrastructures).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime shipping system (oil, diesel, tankers, Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb choke points)
Global AI and advanced-technology ecosystem (model development, safety regimes, big-tech competition)
Global financial markets and monetary/credit system (sovereign yields, bond markets, cross-border capital flows)
Regional security complexes (Indo-Pacific/Taiwan, Middle East/Hormuz, Europe/Eastern Europe)

variables.name: Middle East military escalation
variables.description: Iran, the United States, Gulf states, Saudi-aligned partners and Houthi forces are locked in escalating military and diplomatic confrontations that are altering regional security dynamics.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high-intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with sustained Western military and intelligence support, remain in a prolonged, intensifying war that is reshaping European defence postures and battlefield tactics.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic competition
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting global influence across trade, investment, technology supply chains, arms sales, Arctic/strategic basing and diplomatic alignments, with summit-level engagement shifting tactics without resolving core rivalry.

variables.name: Global energy supply and logistics shock
variables.description: Major producers and consumers are coping with structural fuel shortages, stretched tanker and refining capacity and policy interventions that are driving sustained volatility in fuel markets and supply chains.

variables.name: Global AI governance and competitive race
variables.description: Leading states and technology firms are locked in a rapid competition to develop advanced models and establish international safety, standards and evaluation regimes that will determine technological leadership and regulatory norms.
